body.heading: A star that feels, not smells
paragraphs: The star on this mole's face is not for smelling. Its 22 fleshy rays are touch organs, covered in more than 25,000 minute sensory receptors — far more than cover your entire hand. The mole lives in dark tunnels and wetlands where eyes are nearly useless, so it reads the world by touch instead.

As it travels, the mole presses its star against the ground many times a second, taking tiny tactile snapshots. The outer rays sweep and search, while the small central pair examines anything interesting in fine detail, much the way your eyes flick across a page and then settle on one word.

body.heading: The fastest eater
paragraphs: All that sensing pays off in speed. The star-nosed mole can identify a morsel and decide whether it is food in a fraction of a second, and it holds a record as one of the fastest-eating mammals known. It can even sniff underwater, blowing out bubbles onto an object and breathing them back in to catch its scent.
For an animal that hunts tiny worms and insect larvae in mud and shallow water, hesitation means hunger. The star turns every encounter into instant information.

takeaway: The star-nosed mole explores by touch with over 25,000 sensors, letting it find and judge food in a fraction of a second.
